note: Where the clearings, the thickets and the framed ways into the square belong. Regions are paint: they are applied in file order, so a later region can carve an opening out of an earlier one, and any tile no region covers keeps the seeded variation. Coordinates are tiles.

regions.note: The square and everything you approach it through: paving, the grass ring around it, and the three road mouths. Nothing scatters here, so the landmark and its entrances stay readable.
West lanes. Thin enough to see a long way down the road, so the route out feels open.
South approach from the gate, paired with the lighter ground either side of it.
North-west thicket: the mass you walk around on the way to the café, closing the corner between the treeline and the village.
South-west wood, merged into the boundary treeline at the map's foot.
Inner grove between the square and the south-east water, so the walk out of the square thins into trees as you leave.
Pond shore. Kept open so the water reads and does not disappear under canopy.
North-east meadow, in front of the eastern tree belt. Its job is contrast: dense wood behind, open ground in front.

entrances.note: East road, the way in from Happy Valley.
West road along the shop row.
The southern gate: the widest way in, so it gets the widest arc.
